entities.name: Soil-Transmitted Helminths
entities.description: A major cluster of neglected tropical intestinal nematode infections transmitted through human contact with fecally contaminated soil, predominantly comprising Ascaris lumbricoides, Trichuris trichiura, hookworms (Necator americanus and Ancylostoma duodenale), and Strongyloides stercoralis. The infections manifest with acute transpulmonary larval migration, chronic microcytic iron-deficiency anemia, protein-losing enteropathy, mechanical intestinal or hepatobiliary obstruction, trichuris dysentery with rectal prolapse, and life-threatening disseminated strongyloidiasis in immunosuppressed hosts.

entities.name: Mechanical Intestinal Obstruction
entities.description: Mechanical luminal occlusion of the small intestine, typically the ileocecal valve or distal ileum, caused by an aggregated bolus of adult Ascaris roundworms.

entities.name: Biliary Ascariasis
entities.description: Invasion of adult Ascaris lumbricoides into the biliary tree via the ampulla of Vater, provoking acute biliary colic and choledocholithiasis-like pathology.

entities.name: Acute Cholangitis
entities.description: Suppurative bacterial inflammation and obstruction of the biliary ductal system triggered by wandering intraluminal Ascaris worms and secondary bacterial seeding.

entities.name: Acute Pancreatitis
entities.description: Acute inflammatory injury and enzymatic autodigestion of the pancreas caused by aberrant Ascaris migration into the main pancreatic duct (duct of Wirsung).

entities.name: Hepatic Microabscesses
entities.description: Pyogenic hepatic parenchymal necrotic abscesses formed around decomposing intrahepatic Ascaris worms or entrapped ova.

entities.name: Intestinal Volvulus
entities.description: Pathological axial twisting of a small bowel loop on its mesenteric axis precipitated by the gravitational weight of a heavy intraluminal Ascaris worm bolus.

entities.name: Secondary Intussusception
entities.description: Telescoping of a proximal small bowel segment into an adjacent distal segment with an intraluminal Ascaris worm mass serving as the pathological lead point.

entities.name: Intestinal Perforation
entities.description: Full-thickness breach of the intestinal wall resulting from ischemic pressure necrosis, gangrene, or direct transural worm ulceration.

entities.name: Appendiceal Ascariasis
entities.description: Acute luminally obstructed inflammation of the vermiform appendix triggered by an aberrant adult Ascaris worm lodging inside the appendiceal orifice.

entities.name: Löffler Syndrome
entities.description: Transient allergic eosinophilic pneumonitis provoked by the transpulmonary migration of helminthic larvae breaking through alveolar capillaries.

entities.name: Eosinophilic Pneumonitis
entities.description: Intense inflammatory infiltration of pulmonary interstitial and alveolar spaces by eosinophils responding to migrating larval surface antigens.

entities.name: Bronchospasm
entities.description: Acute reversible bronchoconstriction, expiratory wheezing, and airway hyperresponsiveness triggered by immune complexes during larval lung transit.

entities.name: Hemoptysis
entities.description: Coughing up of blood or blood-streaked sputum resulting from microscopic alveolar capillary hemorrhage caused by penetrating filariform larvae.

entities.name: Chronic Iron-Deficiency Anemia
entities.description: Progressive microcytic hypochromic anemia driven by continuous mechanical ingestion and extravasation of host blood by adult hookworms in the upper intestine.

entities.name: Protein-Losing Enteropathy
entities.description: Massive gastrointestinal protein exudation and enteric albumin wasting caused by diffuse helminth-induced enterocyte disruption and mucosal bleeding.

entities.name: Trichuris Dysentery Syndrome
entities.description: Severe childhood dysenteric illness characterized by chronic mucoid bloody stools, tenesmus, rectal prolapse, and wasting from heavy Trichuris trichiura loads.

entities.name: Rectal Prolapse
entities.description: Circumferential exteriorization of hyperemic edematous rectal mucosa studded with visible white whipworms triggered by excruciating, unrelenting tenesmus.

entities.name: Chronic Colonic Tenesmus
entities.description: Painful, persistent, ineffective straining at stool driven by inflammation and foreign-body irritation of rectal sensory receptors by whipworms.

entities.name: High-Output Heart Failure
entities.description: Hyperdynamic cardiac decompensation characterized by cardiomegaly, tachycardia, and flow murmurs provoked by critical hookworm-induced hemoglobin depletion.

entities.name: Chronic Anasarca
entities.description: Generalized dependent subcutaneous edema and serous cavity effusions driven by profound oncotic pressure collapse secondary to hookworm hypoalbuminemia.

entities.name: Growth Stunting
entities.description: Severe linear growth restriction and irreversible height-for-age deficits resulting from chronic helminthic nutrient diversion and chronic inflammation.

entities.name: Cognitive Impairment
entities.description: Deficits in executive function, verbal processing, memory, and school achievement secondary to chronic cerebral iron starvation in helminthiasis.

entities.name: Pica
entities.description: Pathological craving and compulsive consumption of non-nutritive substances, most commonly soil or clay (geophagia), triggered by severe iron deficiency.

entities.name: Generalized Muscle Fatigue
entities.description: Profound, unremitting physical exhaustion, skeletal muscle asthenia, and reduced daily work capacity due to impaired tissue oxygenation.

entities.name: Exertional Dyspnea
entities.description: Shortness of breath elicited by minimal physical exertion reflecting severely compromised oxygen carrying capacity in advanced hookworm anemia.

entities.name: Strongyloides Hyperinfection Syndrome
entities.description: Explosive internal auto-replication and accelerated dissemination of Strongyloides stercoralis larvae into gut, pulmonary, and extraintestinal tissues.

entities.name: Disseminated Strongyloidiasis
entities.description: Widespread aberrant larval invasion into non-target organs, including the central nervous system, liver, kidneys, pancreas, and skin.

entities.name: Gram-Negative Sepsis
entities.description: Fulminant polymicrobial enteric bacteremia precipitated by invasive Strongyloides larvae carrying gut bacteria across the compromised intestinal wall.

entities.name: Gram-Negative Meningitis
entities.description: Invasive purulent leptomeningitis caused by enteric bacteria transported into the cerebrospinal axis by migrating filariform Strongyloides larvae.

entities.name: Diffuse Alveolar Hemorrhage
entities.description: Extensive pulmonary microvascular shearing and intra-alveolar hemorrhage triggered by thousands of filariform larvae erupting into the bronchial tree.

entities.name: Paralytic Ileus
entities.description: Loss of intestinal peristalsis and neuro-muscular bowel atony provoked by massive transmural larval infiltration and edema in strongyloidiasis.

entities.name: Cutaneous Larva Currens
entities.description: Intensely pruritic, rapidly migrating serpiginous urticarial creeping dermatosis driven by intradermal migration of autoinfective Strongyloides larvae.

entities.name: Chronic Epigastric Pain
entities.description: Burning or aching postprandial dyspepsia localized to the epigastrium resulting from mucosal erosion caused by duodenal hookworm or Strongyloides invasion.

entities.name: Malabsorption Syndrome
entities.description: Impaired intestinal assimilation of fats, fat-soluble vitamins (notably vitamin A), and micronutrients driven by diffuse villous blunting and mucosal inflammation.

entities.name: Digital Clubbing
entities.description: Bulbous enlargement and increased curvature of the nail beds developing in children suffering from chronic heavy Trichuris dysentery syndrome.

entities.name: Biliary Stricture
entities.description: Fibrotic cicatricial narrowing of common or intrahepatic bile ducts developing as a chronic sequela of recurrent ascariasis-induced cholangitis.

entities.name: Recurrent Urticaria
entities.description: Intermittent pruritic cutaneous wheals and erythematous flares elicited by fluctuating circulating helminthic antigen levels and IgE cross-linking.

entities.name: Cholecystitis
entities.description: Acute inflammation of the gallbladder triggered by aberrant wandering Ascaris worms entering the cystic duct or gallbladder lumen.

entities.name: Acute Peritonitis
entities.description: Severe diffuse inflammation of the peritoneal cavity caused by chemical irritation or bacterial contamination from transmural bowel perforation.

entities.name: Hypoalbuminemic Edema
entities.description: Dependent pitting edema of the lower extremities and face driven by diminished plasma oncotic pressure secondary to enteropathic protein loss.

entities.name: Ground Itch
entities.description: Intensely pruritic erythematous papulovesicular dermatitis occurring at the cutaneous entry site of infective hookworm filariform larvae.

entities.name: Visible Rectal Whipworms
entities.description: Direct visual detection of dozens of delicate, thread-like white adult whipworms embedded in prolapsed hyperemic rectal mucosa.

entities.name: Rapidly Advancing Wheal
entities.description: A raised, serpiginous, erythematous urticarial lesion that advances visibly across the skin at a pathognomonic velocity of 5 to 10 cm per hour.

entities.name: Palpable Doughy Abdominal Mass
entities.description: A mobile, non-tender or mildly tender, doughy or sausage-like abdominal mass palpated in the right lower quadrant representing a tangled Ascaris bolus.

entities.name: Severe Conjunctival Pallor
entities.description: Striking porcelain-white bleaching of the lower palpebral conjunctiva signifying critical hemoglobin depletion (< 7 g/dL) in hookworm disease.

entities.name: Koilonychia
entities.description: Concave, spoon-shaped spooning of fingernails with brittle everted edges indicating severe longstanding tissue iron depletion in heavy hookworm infection.

entities.name: Systolic Flow Murmur
entities.description: A harsh or blowing midsystolic ejection murmur heard best over the left sternal border caused by hyperdynamic low-viscosity blood flow in profound anemia.

entities.name: Bounding Peripheral Pulses
entities.description: Wide-pulse-pressure, rapidly rising and collapsing arterial pulses characteristic of the hyperdynamic circulatory state in severe helminthic anemia.

entities.name: Peripheral Pitting Edema
entities.description: Bilateral, symmetrical, dependent pitting edema of the lower extremities reflecting severe hypoalbuminemia from protein-losing enteropathy.

entities.name: Abdominal Distension
entities.description: Prominent, tense, tympanitic abdominal distension observed in pediatric patients with high intestinal Ascaris burdens or complete luminal obstruction.

entities.name: High-Pitched Bowel Sounds
entities.description: Hyperactive, rushing, metallic, high-pitched borborygmi heard on abdominal auscultation corresponding to vigorous peristalsis against a mechanical worm bolus.

entities.name: Palmar Crease Pallor
entities.description: Bleaching and loss of normal pink pigmentation in palmar creases when the fingers are hyperextended, indicating severe hemoglobin depletion (< 7 g/dL).

entities.name: Right Upper Quadrant Tenderness
entities.description: Localized focal tenderness elicited by deep palpation beneath the right costal margin during biliary ascariasis or secondary cholangitis.

entities.name: Positive Murphy Sign
entities.description: Inspiratory arrest elicited by sharp pain when the examiner palpatory fingers compress the gallbladder bed beneath the right costal margin.

entities.name: Scleral Icterus
entities.description: Yellowing of the bulbar conjunctivae and sclerae reflecting extrahepatic biliary tract obstruction caused by intraluminal Ascaris worms.

entities.name: Expiratory Wheezing
entities.description: Diffuse, bilateral, polyphonic expiratory wheezes and prolonged expiration auscultated over the lung fields during larval transpulmonary transit.

entities.name: Fleeting Urticarial Rash
entities.description: Transient, migratory, pruritic erythematous urticarial wheals erupting across the trunk and extremities during the systemic phase of larval migration.

entities.name: Perianal Pruritic Excoriations
entities.description: Erythematous papules and linear skin excoriations around the anal verge and perianal region secondary to intense pruritus from autoinfective larvae.

entities.name: Periumbilical Tenderness
entities.description: Diffuse tenderness to palpation concentrated in the periumbilical zone corresponding to small intestinal distension and worm masses.

entities.name: Involuntary Abdominal Guarding
entities.description: Reflex spasmodic contraction of the abdominal wall musculature on palpation denoting advanced intestinal ischemia, strangulation, or peritonitis.

entities.name: Glossal Papillary Atrophy
entities.description: Smooth, erythematous, depapillated tongue (atrophic glossitis) reflecting chronic severe iron and micronutrient deficiency in heavy hookworm infection.

entities.name: Angular Cheilitis
entities.description: Erythematous, macerated, painful fissures at the oral commissures resulting from chronic severe iron deficiency anemia.

entities.name: Pale Palpebral Conjunctivae
entities.description: Significant pallor and blanching of the palpebral and bulbar conjunctivae on eye inspection indicating substantial red cell loss.

entities.name: Hepatosplenomegaly
entities.description: Concurrent enlargement of the liver and spleen detected by abdominal palpation in chronic heavy pediatric Trichuris dysentery or severe hookworm disease.

entities.name: Periorbital Puffiness
entities.description: Bilateral, non-erythematous subcutaneous fluid accumulation and puffiness around the eyes resulting from severe hypoproteinemia.

entities.name: Visible Peristaltic Waves
entities.description: Hypertrophied small intestinal peristaltic contractions contouring visibly beneath a thin abdominal wall in children with mechanical worm obstruction.

entities.name: Crepitant Pulmonary Rales
entities.description: Fine inspiratory crackles auscultated over the mid and lower lung zones during the acute alveolitis of Löffler syndrome.

entities.name: Waxy Facial Pallor
entities.description: An unmistakable alabaster, yellowish-waxy, pale facial complexion characteristic of profound, longstanding hookworm-induced anemia.

entities.name: Microcytic Hypochromic Anemia
entities.description: Marked reduction in hemoglobin (< 7 g/dL) and hematocrit accompanied by profound microcytosis (MCV < 70 fL) and hypochromia (MCH < 22 pg).

entities.name: Low Serum Ferritin
entities.description: Depleted systemic iron stores indicated by serum ferritin concentrations plunging below 10-15 ng/mL.

entities.name: Elevated Total Iron-Binding Capacity
entities.description: Compensatory increase in circulating transferrin producing an elevated TIBC (> 400 mcg/dL) and profoundly depressed transferrin saturation (< 10%).

entities.name: Marked Peripheral Eosinophilia
entities.description: Massive increase in circulating absolute eosinophil counts (20-50% differential, > 1,500-3,000 cells/mcL) during acute tissue-invasive larval phases.

entities.name: Mild Chronic Eosinophilia
entities.description: Persistent, low-grade elevation in circulating eosinophils (5-15% differential) characteristic of established adult luminal intestinal helminthiasis.

entities.name: Severe Hypoalbuminemia
entities.description: Depression of serum albumin concentrations below 2.5 g/dL resulting from mucosal exudation, intestinal hemorrhage, and protein-losing enteropathy.

entities.name: Elevated Serum IgE
entities.description: Marked polyclonal elevation in circulating immunoglobulin E concentrations (> 1,000 IU/mL) stimulated by helminthic antigens and Th2 immune skewing.

entities.name: Kato-Katz Stool Microscopy
entities.description: Standardized quantitative cellophane fecal thick smear examination providing direct visualization of helminth eggs and quantification of infection intensity.

entities.name: Mammillated Ascaris Eggs
entities.description: Microscopic visualization of large, golden-brown, thick-shelled oval ova (45-75 x 35-50 mcm) coated with a bumpy, mammillated albuminous outer layer.

entities.name: Bipolar Plugged Eggs
entities.description: Microscopic detection of unmistakable barrel-shaped or football-shaped golden-brown ova (50-55 x 22-24 mcm) with prominent transparent bipolar mucoid plugs.

entities.name: Thin-Shelled Hookworm Ova
entities.description: Microscopic identification of oval, transparent, thin-shelled eggs (60-75 x 35-40 mcm) containing a developing 4-to-8-cell morula.

entities.name: Baermann Funnel Concentration
entities.description: Specialized thermo-hydrotropic fecal concentration method that induces motile nematode larvae to migrate through warm water for diagnostic recovery.

entities.name: Koga Agar Plate Culture
entities.description: Diagnostic fecal culture on nutrient agar where living Strongyloides larvae crawl across the plate carrying enteric bacteria that form visible tracking colonies.

entities.name: Motile Rhabditiform Larvae
entities.description: Microscopic visualization of actively writhing first-stage (L1) larvae (200-300 mcm) with a short buccal cavity and prominent genital primordium in fresh stool.

entities.name: Strongyloides IgG ELISA
entities.description: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay demonstrating elevated serum IgG antibodies directed against Strongyloides filariform larval crude antigens.

entities.name: Elevated Serum Bilirubin
entities.description: Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia reflecting mechanical extrahepatic biliary outflow obstruction caused by intraluminal Ascaris worms.

entities.name: Elevated Alkaline Phosphatase
entities.description: Marked elevation in serum alkaline phosphatase and gamma-glutamyl transferase denoting biliary ductal epithelial irritation and cholestasis.

entities.name: Elevated Serum Lipase
entities.description: Threefold or greater increase in serum lipase and amylase concentrations confirming acute pancreatitis induced by ampullary Ascaris impaction.

entities.name: Fecal Occult Blood
entities.description: Positive chemical or immunochemical stool testing demonstrating continuous microvascular mucosal bleeding from hookworm lacerations.

entities.name: Polyclonal Gram-Negative Bacteremia
entities.description: Blood cultures yielding enteric bacilli (Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Enterobacter) transported across the gut barrier by Strongyloides larvae.

entities.name: Polymicrobial CSF Pleocytosis
entities.description: Cerebrospinal fluid showing elevated neutrophil pleocytosis, high protein, low glucose, and Gram-negative bacilli transported by larvae.

entities.name: Elevated C-Reactive Protein
entities.description: Marked elevation of systemic inflammatory biomarkers (CRP > 50 mg/L and high ESR) reflecting secondary bacterial peritonitis, cholangitis, or sepsis.

entities.name: Ultrasound Strip Sign
entities.description: Sonographic visualization of a non-shadowing, linear, hyperechoic tubular structure with an anechoic central longitudinal line within the common bile duct.

entities.name: Ultrasound Inner Tube Sign
entities.description: Transverse sonographic cross-section of an Ascaris worm in the common bile duct showing a circular hyperechoic rim surrounding an anechoic central lumen.

entities.name: Ultrasound Spaghetti Sign
entities.description: Sonographic appearance of multiple clustered, non-shadowing, parallel echogenic tubular interfaces within dilated bowel loops representing coiled worms.

entities.name: Real-Time Worm Motility
entities.description: Dynamic bedside ultrasound visualization of slow writhing, coiling, and active longitudinal curling movements of living Ascaris worms.

entities.name: Common Bile Duct Dilation
entities.description: Ultrasound measurement demonstrating substantial extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation (> 8-10 mm) proximal to an obstructing intraluminal Ascaris worm.

entities.name: Gallbladder Sludge and Distension
entities.description: Sonographic identification of marked gallbladder hydrops, thickened wall, and echogenic biliary sludge resulting from cystic duct obstruction.

entities.name: Railroad Track Sign
entities.description: Abdominal radiography or barium contrast meal demonstrating parallel radiolucent cylindrical filling defects representing long adult roundworms.

entities.name: Dilated Small Bowel Loops
entities.description: Erect and supine abdominal radiographs showing multiple distended loops of small bowel (> 3 cm caliber) with prominent air-fluid levels.

entities.name: Fleeting Pulmonary Infiltrates
entities.description: Plain chest radiography showing patchy, non-segmental, migratory fluffy alveolar opacities that spontaneously resolve over 1 to 2 weeks.

entities.name: Diffuse Alveolar Infiltrates
entities.description: Chest radiography and CT showing bilateral diffuse ground-glass or dense airspace consolidation during fulminant Strongyloides hyperinfection.

entities.name: Barium Meal Filling Defect
entities.description: Smooth, elongated, cylindrical radiolucent filling defect within the small intestine produced by contrast passing around an adult Ascaris worm.

entities.name: Abdominal Free Air
entities.description: Subdiaphragmatic crescentic radiolucency (pneumoperitoneum) seen on upright chest or abdominal radiograph confirming visceral perforation.

entities.name: Target Sign on Ultrasound
entities.description: Transverse sonographic cross-section of intussuscepted bowel exhibiting concentric alternating hyperechoic and hypoechoic rings.

entities.name: High Kato-Katz Egg Count
entities.description: Quantitative fecal smear egg counts exceeding high-intensity thresholds: > 50,000 epg for Ascaris, > 4,000 epg for hookworm, > 10,000 epg for Trichuris.

entities.name: Bronchoalveolar Lavage Eosinophils
entities.description: Cytological analysis of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid demonstrating marked eosinophilia (> 25% of total cells) and occasional migrating nematode larvae.

entities.name: Stool Charcot-Leyden Crystals
entities.description: Microscopic detection of hexagonal bipyramidal crystals composed of lysophospholipase released by degranulating intestinal eosinophils.

entities.name: Barefoot Soil Contact
entities.description: Direct physical contact between bare skin (feet, ankles) and warm, moist, fecally contaminated soil containing infective filariform larvae.

entities.name: Contaminated Raw Produce
entities.description: Ingestion of unwashed, uncooked vegetables and fruits cultivated in soil contaminated with viable embryonated eggs.

entities.name: Untreated Drinking Water
entities.description: Consumption of non-potable surface or shallow well water contaminated with human fecal runoff harboring embryonated helminth eggs.

entities.name: Human Nightsoil Fertilizer
entities.description: Agricultural utilization of raw, uncomposted human feces as crop fertilizer, directly dispersing massive helminth egg loads into topsoil.

entities.name: Inadequate Municipal Sanitation
entities.description: Residence in impoverished communities lacking sewage collection, flush latrines, and sanitary waste disposal infrastructure.

entities.name: Open Defecation Practices
entities.description: Habitual outdoor defecation in agricultural fields, bushes, and ditch banks, directly contaminating the immediate soil environment with helminth ova.

entities.name: Geophagia Soil Ingestion
entities.description: Deliberate or compulsive ingestion of soil or clay, common in young children and pregnant women, directly transmitting embryonated eggs.

entities.name: Tropical Climate Conditions
entities.description: Environmental conditions of warm temperature (20-30°C), high humidity, shade, and loose moisture-retentive soil required for embryonation.

entities.name: School-Age Children
entities.description: Pediatric demographic (ages 5 to 14 years) harboring the highest prevalence, heaviest worm intensities, and highest morbidity burden.

entities.name: Preschool-Age Children
entities.description: Young children (ages 1 to 4 years) at elevated risk of mechanical Ascaris obstruction, acute trichuris dysentery, and irreversible developmental delay.

entities.name: Pregnant Women
entities.description: Gravid females experiencing compounded physiological iron demands who suffer severe hookworm anemia leading to low birth weight and maternal death.

entities.name: Agricultural Tea Pickers
entities.description: Plantation laborers working barefoot in humid, shaded tea and coffee estates with hyperendemic ground contamination by hookworm larvae.

entities.name: Underground Mine Workers
entities.description: Subterranean miners working in warm, damp, non-sanitated tunnel systems that provide optimal microclimates for Ancylostoma duodenale larvae.

entities.name: Immunosuppressed Transplant Recipients
entities.description: Solid organ or stem cell allograft recipients receiving potent immunosuppression at extreme risk of fulminant Strongyloides hyperinfection.

entities.name: Systemic Corticosteroid Therapy
entities.description: Patients receiving systemic glucocorticoids, which directly stimulate Strongyloides ecdysteroid receptors, driving fulminant autoinfection.

entities.name: HTLV-1 Infection
entities.description: Coinfection with Human T-cell Lymphotropic Virus Type 1, which skews cytokine production towards IFN-gamma and suppresses protective Th2 defenses.

entities.name: Hematologic Malignancy Patients
entities.description: Patients with lymphoma, leukemia, or multiple myeloma suffering profound cell-mediated immune impairment permitting uncontrolled larval propagation.

entities.name: Pulmonary Larval Incubation
entities.description: The biological latency interval of 7 to 14 days between percutaneous larval invasion or egg ingestion and acute transpulmonary migration.

entities.name: Ascaris Prepatent Period
entities.description: The developmental timeframe of 60 to 75 days required from infective egg ingestion to sexual maturity and egg detection in feces.

entities.name: Hookworm Prepatent Period
entities.description: The biological interval of 5 to 9 weeks from percutaneous larval penetration to adult worm mating and egg production in the intestine.

entities.name: Trichuris Prepatent Period
entities.description: The developmental duration of 60 to 90 days required from whipworm egg ingestion to adult worm establishment in the cecal epithelium and oviposition.

entities.name: Strongyloides Decadal Longevity
entities.description: The lifelong persistence of infection spanning 30 to 50+ years maintained exclusively through continuous internal autoinfection cycles.

entities.name: Acute Septic Shock
entities.description: Hyperacute cardiovascular collapse with refractory hypotension, cool extremities, and lactic acidosis developing within hours.

entities.name: Hyperacute Febrile Toxemia
entities.description: Sudden onset of high spiking fevers (> 39.5°C) accompanied by profound prostration, rigors, and delirium within 24 hours.

entities.name: Completely Normal Hemoglobin
entities.description: Entirely normal red cell mass and normal hemoglobin concentration (> 13 g/dL in males, > 12 g/dL in females) with normal MCV.

entities.name: Normal Absolute Eosinophils
entities.description: Absolute eosinophil count strictly within normal limits (< 350-500 cells/mcL) in a patient presenting with acute pulmonary infiltrates.

entities.name: Multiple Negative Stool Exams
entities.description: Absence of helminth eggs and larvae across three serial concentrated fecal examinations using Kato-Katz and Baermann methods.

entities.name: Sterile Non-Eosinophilic Pyuria
entities.description: Urine showing persistent leukocytes with negative standard bacterial cultures and absent eosinophils or microhematuria.

entities.name: Massive Bloody Emesis
entities.description: Sudden, voluminous hematemesis with hemodynamic instability indicating rupture of upper gastrointestinal or esophageal varices.

entities.name: Watery Rice-Water Stools
entities.description: Massive, effortless, painless, voluminous watery diarrhea with flecks of mucus resembling rice-water, driving rapid hypovolemic collapse.

entities.name: Maculopapular Centripetal Exanthem
entities.description: A generalized erythematous maculopapular cutaneous eruption spreading centripetally from extremities to trunk or associated with an eschar.

entities.name: Focal Neurologic Deficits
entities.description: Acute focal neurological signs such as hemiplegia, aphasia, or cranial nerve palsies occurring without severe disseminated sepsis.

entities.name: Severe Thrombocytopenia
entities.description: Profound, acute depression of peripheral blood platelet count (< 50,000/mcL) in a febrile patient.

entities.name: Markedly Elevated Ferritin
entities.description: Serum ferritin concentrations exceeding 1,000 to 5,000 ng/mL reflecting massive macrophage activation, hemophagocytosis, or adult Still disease.

entities.name: Direct Person-to-Person Transmission
entities.description: Immediate transmission between household members within hours of contact, without environmental soil incubation.

entities.name: Rapid Symptom Onset
entities.description: Development of acute gastroenteritis, vomiting, and diarrhea within 2 to 12 hours following a suspected dietary exposure.

entities.name: Non-Pitting Lymphedema
entities.description: Chronic, non-pitting, hard, brawny elephantiasis with dermal hyperkeratosis and mossy papillomatosis of the lower extremities.

entities.name: Unsegmented Non-Gram-Negative Meningitis
entities.description: Meningitis demonstrating pure lymphocytic CSF pleocytosis with isolation of cryptococci, viruses, or typical Gram-positive diplococci.

entities.name: Continuous Unremitting Pyrexia
entities.description: High, sustained, step-ladder fever persisting for weeks without respiratory or bowel obstruction in an endemic resident.

entities.name: Absence of Anemia
entities.description: Sustained normal red blood cell indices, normal MCV, and normal hemoglobin in a patient with chronic severe lethargy.

entities.name: Left Shift Neutrophilia
entities.description: Marked leukocytosis (> 20,000/mcL) with high bandemia (> 15% bands) and toxic granulations in the complete absence of eosinophils.

entities.name: Elevated Procalcitonin
entities.description: Serum procalcitonin markedly elevated (> 2.0 to 10 ng/mL) indicating severe invasive systemic bacterial infection.

entities.name: Negative Strongyloides Serology
entities.description: High-sensitivity IgG ELISA antibodies directed against Strongyloides antigen testing negative in an immunocompetent patient.

entities.name: Stationarily Clustered Burrows
entities.description: Static, non-advancing linear scabetic burrows localized strictly to web spaces, flexor wrists, and genitalia with nocturnal itching.

entities.name: Nutritional Iron Deficiency
entities.description: Microcytic hypochromic anemia caused by inadequate dietary iron intake without ongoing intestinal parasitic blood loss.

entities.name: Bacillary Dysentery
entities.description: Acute invasive inflammatory colitis caused by Shigella species characterized by high fever, toxic appearance, and bloody mucoid stools.

entities.name: Acute Appendicitis
entities.description: Bacterial inflammation and suppurative necrosis of the appendix typically initiated by fecaliths or lymphoid hyperplasia.

entities.name: Idiopathic Intussusception
entities.description: Idiopathic or anatomical invagination of bowel loops in infants, typically characterized by red currant jelly stools and target signs on ultrasound.

entities.name: Intestinal Tuberculosis
entities.description: Chronic granulomatous Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the ileocecal region causing transmural strictures and lymphadenopathy.

entities.name: Choledocholithiasis
entities.description: Gallstones lodged within the common bile duct causing acoustic shadowing, ductal dilation, and obstructive jaundice.

entities.name: Bronchial Asthma
entities.description: Chronic atopic inflammatory airway disease characterized by episodic reversible bronchoconstriction without migratory radiographic opacities.

entities.name: Cutaneous Larva Migrans
entities.description: Self-limited creeping dermatitis caused by animal hookworms (Ancylostoma braziliense) advancing slowly (1-2 cm/day) in epidermal layers.

entities.name: Sarcoptes Scabiei Infestation
entities.description: Ectoparasitic mite infestation producing stationary pruritic burrows in finger webs, flexor surfaces, and external genitalia.

entities.name: Amoebic Dysentery
entities.description: Protozoan invasive colitis caused by Entamoeba histolytica featuring flask-shaped ulcers, trophozoites with ingested red cells, and liver abscesses.

entities.name: Celiac Disease
entities.description: Autoimmune enteropathy triggered by gluten ingestion leading to blunting of duodenal villi and elevated anti-tissue transglutaminase antibodies.

entities.name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease
entities.description: Chronic idiopathic inflammatory bowel disorder (ulcerative colitis or Crohn disease) causing mucosal ulceration and non-caseating granulomas.

entities.name: Acute Viral Hepatitis
entities.description: Hepatocellular viral infection (HAV, HBV, HEV) causing massive acute transaminitis (> 1,000 U/L) without mechanical biliary obstruction.

entities.name: Tropical Pulmonary Eosinophilia
entities.description: Severe hypersensitivity response to microfilariae of Wuchereria bancrofti or Brugia malayi causing chronic nocturnal asthma and high-titer filarial antibodies.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, untreated drinking water, contaminated water source, surface runoff, embryonated eggs
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is acquired via exposure to untreated drinking water contaminated with human excreta containing hardy, infective embryonated eggs of Ascaris lumbricoides.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, human nightsoil, fecal fertilizer, agricultural soil, helminth transmission
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is acquired through agricultural exposure to human nightsoil fertilizer, which seeds farmlands with millions of durable embryonated Ascaris and Trichuris eggs.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, inadequate sanitation, lack of latrines, sewage infrastructure, environmental contamination

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, open defecation, environmental contamination, soil seeding, parasite life cycle
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is sustained by exposure to open defecation practices in rural communities, which continuously replenishes infective eggs and larvae in topsoil.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, geophagia, soil ingestion, pica behavior, direct egg inoculation

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, tropical climate, warm moist soil, environmental embryonation, parasite ecology
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Soil-Transmitted Helminths depends upon exposure to tropical climate conditions, where warm temperatures, moisture, and dense canopy shade provide obligatory conditions for egg embryonation.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, school-age children, pediatric host, heavy worm burden, deworming target
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Soil-Transmitted Helminths targets school-age children as the primary high-risk host group, who harbor the highest worm burdens of Ascaris and Trichuris and suffer severe physical and cognitive stunting.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, preschool-age children, toddlers, intestinal obstruction risk, pediatric vulnerability
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Soil-Transmitted Helminths identifies preschool-age children as a critically vulnerable high-risk host group, where small intestinal caliber predisposes to catastrophic mechanical Ascaris obstruction.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, pregnant women, maternal morbidity, hookworm anemia, low birth weight
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Soil-Transmitted Helminths identifies pregnant women as an essential high-risk host population, in whom hookworm blood loss exacerbates maternal anemia, dramatically increasing perinatal and maternal mortality.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, tea pickers, plantation workers, occupational exposure, hookworm transmission
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Soil-Transmitted Helminths targets agricultural tea pickers as an occupational high-risk host group, who experience prolonged daily barefoot exposure to shaded, damp soil harboring hookworm larvae.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, underground miners, mine shafts, Ancylostoma duodenale, occupational risk
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Soil-Transmitted Helminths historically and currently targets underground mine workers as high-risk hosts for Ancylostoma duodenale, thriving in dark, warm, humid subterranean shafts.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, transplant recipients, allograft immunosuppression, Strongyloides hyperinfection, fatal sepsis

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, systemic corticosteroids, glucocorticoids, ecdysteroid receptors, hyperinfection trigger

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, HTLV-1 coinfection, Th2 suppression, impaired anthelmintic defense, disseminated strongyloidiasis
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Soil-Transmitted Helminths targets individuals with HTLV-1 infection as high-risk hosts, in whom retroviral impairment of Th2 eosinophilic responses causes intractable, recurring strongyloidiasis.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, hematologic malignancy, lymphoma, leukemia, cellular immunodeficiency, Strongyloides
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Soil-Transmitted Helminths identifies hematologic malignancy patients as high-risk hosts who are exceptionally prone to lethal Strongyloides dissemination during cytotoxic chemotherapy.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, pulmonary incubation, larval migration timing, Löffler syndrome latency
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Soil-Transmitted Helminths exhibits a pulmonary larval incubation period of 7 to 14 days, during which ingested Ascaris ova or percutaneous hookworm/Strongyloides larvae traverse pulmonary tissue.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, Ascaris prepatent period, maturation timeline, adult roundworm patency
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Soil-Transmitted Helminths exhibits an Ascaris prepatent period of 60 to 75 days, spanning the interval from initial embryonated egg ingestion to the excretion of mature diagnostic ova in stool.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, hookworm prepatent period, larval development, adult worm maturation
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Soil-Transmitted Helminths exhibits a hookworm prepatent period of 5 to 9 weeks, required for filariform larvae to migrate through lungs, mature in the duodenum, and release eggs.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, Trichuris prepatent period, whipworm maturation, cecal establishment
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Soil-Transmitted Helminths exhibits a Trichuris prepatent period of 60 to 90 days, reflecting the slow maturation of whipworms within the crypts of the cecum and proximal colon.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, decadal longevity, chronic autoinfection, lifelong persistence, Strongyloides
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Soil-Transmitted Helminths demonstrates decadal longevity in Strongyloides stercoralis infections, where internal autoinfection cycles permit indefinite survival inside human hosts for 30 to 50 years.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, acute septic shock, hyperacute hypotension, bacterial endotoxemia, exclusion boundary

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, hyperacute febrile toxemia, high spiking fever, bacterial prostration, non-helminthic illness
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is ruled out by hyperacute febrile toxemia with prostration and high swinging fevers, which points to acute pyogenic bacterial infections or severe falciparum malaria.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, normal hemoglobin, normal hematocrit, absence of anemia, rules out heavy hookworm

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, normal eosinophil count, absence of eosinophilia, rules out Löffler syndrome
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is ruled out as the cause of acute pulmonary symptoms by normal absolute eosinophils, which strongly excludes active Löffler syndrome and acute tissue-invasive helminthiasis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, negative stool exams, absence of eggs, serial Kato-Katz negative, exclusion of STH
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is ruled out by multiple negative stool exams using concentrated Kato-Katz and Baermann techniques, effectively excluding heavy symptomatic luminal helminthic infection.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, sterile pyuria, negative urine culture, non-eosinophilic pyuria, exclusion sign
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is ruled out by sterile non-eosinophilic pyuria, which directs clinical evaluation toward renal tuberculosis, interstitial nephritis, or genitourinary schistosomiasis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, massive bloody emesis, variceal bleeding, hematemesis, non-helminthic upper GI bleed

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, rice-water stools, massive secretory diarrhea, Vibrio cholerae, exclusion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is ruled out by watery rice-water stools with profound hypovolemic dehydration, characteristic of epidemic Vibrio cholerae rather than subacute helminthic enteropathy.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, maculopapular exanthem, rickettsial rash, scrub typhus eschar, exclusion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is ruled out by a generalized maculopapular centripetal exanthem or cutaneous eschar, which indicates acute rickettsiosis or viral exanthems rather than helminth ground itch.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, focal neurologic deficits, stroke-like presentation, intracranial mass lesion, neurocysticercosis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is ruled out by acute focal neurologic deficits, which point toward acute ischemic stroke, cerebral malaria, or neurocysticercosis rather than intestinal nematode infection.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, severe thrombocytopenia, low platelets, dengue, malaria, acute infection

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, elevated ferritin, hyperferritinemia, macrophage activation, exclusion of hookworm

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, person-to-person transmission, direct contagion, immediate infectivity, rules out STH

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, rapid symptom onset, foodborne toxin, preformed enterotoxin, acute incubation
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is ruled out by rapid symptom onset within hours of dietary ingestion, which points to preformed bacterial enterotoxins rather than the prolonged prepatent periods of STH.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, non-pitting lymphedema, elephantiasis, lymphatic filariasis, brawny edema
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is ruled out by chronic non-pitting lymphedema and elephantiasis, which is diagnostic of lymphatic filariasis or podoconiosis rather than intestinal soil-transmitted helminths.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, aseptic meningitis, fungal meningitis, non-enteric meningitis, exclusion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is ruled out by pure lymphocytic or non-enteric meningitis, which excludes Strongyloides hyperinfection-associated enteric bacteremic translocation.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, absence of anemia, normal red cells, rules out hookworm morbidity

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, left shift neutrophilia, toxic granulations, bandemia, bacterial pyogenic infection

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, elevated procalcitonin, high procalcitonin, invasive bacterial sepsis, non-parasitic marker

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, stationary burrows, web space lesions, scabies burrows, non-migratory lesion

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, cutaneous larva migrans, Ancylostoma braziliense, creeping eruption, slow migration

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, amoebic dysentery, Entamoeba histolytica, flask ulcers, Trichuris trichiura, whipworm
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is differentiated from amoebic dysentery by stool microscopy demonstrating barrel-shaped bipolar Trichuris eggs, absence of hematophagous amoebic trophozoites, and lack of amebic seropositivity or hepatic abscesses.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, celiac disease, anti-tTG IgA, gluten enteropathy, helminth malabsorption, reversible enteropathy
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is differentiated from celiac disease by negative anti-tissue transglutaminase (tTG) IgA serology, presence of helminth ova or larvae in stool, and complete reversal of enteropathy following anthelmintic deworming.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, inflammatory bowel disease, ulcerative colitis, Crohn disease, Trichuris dysentery, whipworm biopsy
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is differentiated from ulcerative colitis by direct visualization of adult whipworms embedded in prolapsed rectal mucosa, absence of chronic crypt architectural distortion, and curative response to mebendazole.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, acute viral hepatitis, transaminitis, non-obstructive jaundice, biliary ascariasis, ultrasound strip sign
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is differentiated from acute viral hepatitis by normal or moderately elevated aminotransferases, an obstructive alkaline phosphatase elevation, and sonographic visualization of intraluminal Ascaris worms.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, tropical pulmonary eosinophilia, lymphatic filariasis, nocturnal paroxysms, Löffler syndrome, self-limited course

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, eosinophilic gastroenteritis, idiopathic enteritis, anthelmintic response, Kato-Katz stool exam
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is differentiated from idiopathic eosinophilic gastroenteritis by recovery of helminth eggs or larvae on concentrated stool analysis and permanent cure following targeted anthelmintic therapy.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, chronic giardiasis, Giardia lamblia, flagellated trophozoites, hookworm anemia, stool microscopy
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is differentiated from chronic giardiasis by the absence of protozoan cysts or trophozoites on microscopy, absence of profound hookworm-induced microcytic anemia in giardiasis, and specific response to benzimidazoles.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, acute mesenteric adenitis, lymph node clustering, Yersinia, palpable worm bolus, ultrasound
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is differentiated from acute mesenteric adenitis by ultrasound revealing a palpable intraluminal tangled mass of adult worms rather than clusters of enlarged, hyperemic mesenteric lymph nodes.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, EGPA, Churg-Strauss syndrome, necrotizing vasculitis, ANCA positive, Löffler syndrome
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Soil-Transmitted Helminths is differentiated from eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) by negative ANCA antibodies, absence of multiorgan necrotizing vasculitis, and transient non-destructive nature of helminthic Löffler pneumonitis.
